study_identification_part.si3_author_journal_year: Elad et al., Human Brain Mapping, 2021
study_identification_part.si4_title: Improving the predictive potential of diffusion MRI in schizophrenia using normative models - Towards subject-level classification

cm1_research_objectives.reason: The study's objectives are clearly stated: to evaluate the predictive power of features derived from a normative modeling approach compared to raw dMRI values for classifying schizophrenia subjects, motivated by the hypothesis that common abnormalities may occur in spatially distinct regions.
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: In this article, we use a large sample of harmonized dMRI data... to evaluate the predictive power of features derived from a normative modeling approach and compare it with the predictive power of raw dMRI values serving as features. Here, our motivation is to improve the characterization of the schizophrenia group as a whole by assuming that common abnormalities (e.g., decreased FA/FAt, increased FW) may occur in spatially distinct regions across subjects.

nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.reason: The study uses a previously published harmonized dataset. The authors cite the original publication for the complete account of inclusion/exclusion criteria and report the final sample size (512 healthy controls).
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.supporting_text: The dataset used in this study coincides with the dataset utilized in the published work by (Cetin-Karayumak et al., 2020)... A complete account of demographics, inclusion and exclusion criteria, acquisition protocols across the 13 sites, preprocessing and harmonization procedures can be found in Cetin-Karayumak et al. (2020). ... 512 healthy controls

nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.reason: The study explicitly handles age and sex. Normative models are estimated for each sex separately, and age is used as a covariate in the Nadaraya-Watson estimator. Site effects were handled by retrospective harmonization prior to analysis.
nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.supporting_text: To control for confounding factors resulting from age and sex differences, we represented the normative range in each ROI by an age specific weighted mean, c mh , and standard deviation, b σ 2 h , for each sex separately. ... The single shell dMRI data... were harmonized across sites to remove site-related differences using retrospective harmonization (Karayumak et al., 2019; Ning et al., 2020).

nm5_data_preprocessing.reason: The preprocessing procedures are described, including the software used (FSL, ANTs) and the models fitted (DTI, Free-water). The use of a standardized protocol and harmonization is mentioned.
nm5_data_preprocessing.supporting_text: The harmonized data were fitted using FSL's DTIFIT (Behrens et al., 2003) to the DTI model, from which FA was derived. The data were also fitted to the two-compartments Free-water imaging model... The FA image of each subject was registered to the FA IIT template using ANTs registration (Avants et al., 2011)...

nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: To set h for every ROI... we minimized the cross-validation function... where ... is the leave-one-out-estimator... The same procedure was also used to evaluate deviation of each healthy control subject, but with a leave-one-out approach

nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: Prediction performance of the estimated models was validated using a 10-fold cross-validation procedure. The data were partitioned into 10 subsets...

nm8_normative_modeling_approach.supporting_text: To control for confounding factors... we used the NadarayaWatson (NW) estimator (Nadaraya, 1964; Watson, 1964) with a Gaussian kernel... To set h for every ROI... we minimized the cross-validation function

cr6_interpretation_of_deviation_scores.reason: The interpretation of deviation scores (z-scores) is explained. A threshold for defining abnormality (|z| > 2.999) is reported and justified (Bonferroni correction). The clinical implications of using extreme deviations versus the full distribution are discussed.
cr6_interpretation_of_deviation_scores.supporting_text: Deviations are typically quantified using a z -score... abnormalities are identified as those values that are outliers... To define abnormal z -scores we used the threshold of | z | > 2.999... Our findings suggest that extreme deviations from a normative model are not optimal features for prediction.
